analysis.title: ETD Rates Watch: Equity Futures Rebound As Markets Digest Democratic Sweep
key_insights: News of a Democratic sweep of the Senate and House pushed E-mini S&P 500 futures down 1.63% at the lows (7,490) in the Wednesday Asia session. Dip buyers then lifted the market 1.24% off the lows. E-mini Nasdaq futures followed the same pattern.
The Kospi rallied 3.2% on the open, fell 4%, then recovered to +0.62% as of 0705 GMT. The desk calls the first move in markets not always the right one.
Fixed income rallied initially on equity weakness and then gave back the gains. Front-end pricing is little changed, with 19.3bp of hikes priced for December, roughly unchanged from Tuesday.

Futures volumes were almost three times the recent average, with TY trading 452k. Options activity was quiet by recent standards, and no strike in regular TY expiries had traded over 5,000 lots as of 0710 GMT.

Markets now have two things to focus on: Iran and the AI trade. Trump told the Financial Times the US had no plans to strike Iran and said he was content with the stand-off, which raised headlines around a possible deal.

Data-centre policy is a new concern for tech. Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa campaigned on an immediate moratorium on data-centre development. The desk notes data-centre investment has been a major driver of US growth and may have masked the effect of higher energy prices.
A possible offset to a data-centre slowdown is a pickup in housebuilding if resources are redeployed. The desk says the implications for the Fed will not be answered today.

ECB Governing Council member Nagel said the ECB would probably raise rates next month because inflation has worsened since the September forecasts and repeated energy spikes raise second-round risks. Kocher echoed this.
Accounts are focusing on the 97.0625 strike in ERH7, positioning for December to be the last hike of the cycle. About 50k of the ERH7 96.6875/96.8125/97.0625/97.1875 call condor has accumulated.

Private credit concern looks limited. Blackstone raised about EUR 13bn for its European direct lending strategy, and Ares is raising money faster for its latest US direct lending fund than for the previous record vintage.

China was the best-performing Asian equity market, with the Shanghai Composite up 2.16% and Shenzhen Composite up 3.7%, as state-backed funds stepped in. A basket of ETFs favoured by state funds took in $11.5bn on Tuesday, the second-largest inflow on record.

sector_views.rationale: The desk flags concern over a possible halt to data-centre construction after the election, given the sector's contribution to US growth. It notes the dip was bought in Asia hours.

macro_indicators.indicator: Fed rate hikes priced for December
macro_indicators.interpretation: Market pricing of Fed hikes is little changed from Tuesday, so the election result has not shifted front-end expectations.
Nagel said the ECB would probably raise rates, and the only way to avoid it is a dramatic change in the inflation picture.

risk_factors: Possible halt to data-centre construction after Democratic wins at state and federal level, which would remove a major driver of US growth.
Higher energy prices, which the desk suggests AI-related growth has helped mask.
Iran stand-off, with the outcome of a possible deal still unresolved.
ECB second-round inflation effects from repeated energy price spikes.
vol_and_positioning: TY futures volume was 452k, almost three times the recent average, while options were quiet. No strike in regular TY expiries traded over 5,000 lots as of 0710 GMT.
In FV, upside remained the preferred play. The FVZ6 104.75/105.75/106.50 broken call fly was bought for 17.5 in 2k, and also bought against selling the 104.25 put for 6.5.

In SOFR options, a buyer took 4k 1y March midcurve 96/96.50 call spreads for 8, with underlying SFRH8 at 95.535. SOFR futures spreads were more active, with SFRH7/M7 (12.13) trading 10k and SFRM7/Z7 (1.5/2) trading 8.5k.

In euribor options, about 50k of the ERH7 96.6875/96.8125/97.0625/97.1875 call condor has accumulated, first bought for 6.5 on Tuesday. Accounts are positioning for December to be the last hike of the cycle.
geopolitical: Democrats took both the Senate and the House. Trump congratulated them, acknowledged the Iran war contributed to his defeat, and said he would use his veto in the last two years of his term.
Trump told the Financial Times the US had no plans to strike Iran. Ghalibaf, speaker of the Iranian parliament, said the Republican defeat was America saying no to war.

tension_points.bull_case: Dip buyers bought the post-election equity drop within the Asia session, and a halt to data-centre building could be partly offset by housebuilding if resources are redeployed.
tension_points.bear_case: Data-centre development has been a major tailwind for US growth and may have masked higher energy prices. Campaigns such as Hinojosa's in Texas called for an immediate moratorium.
